title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). They were deliberately NOT changed: completeElidedBeacons and completeTruncatedBeacon are load-bearing for many character-locked scenarios (S27, S28, S30 among others) and already carry their own retiming logic — completeElidedBeacons re-times the BEACON backward when its seed precedes it — so extending the clamp without a reproducer risks breaking locked ground truths to fix a defect nobody has observed. REQUIRE a reproducing scenario that shows one of these two stampers emitting an out-of-order seed BEFORE changing them; then reuse the existing clamp and run the full suite.

title: Fixture mode: serve the REAL Layer 1 page from canned payloads, so the mockup stops needing to be kept in sync
description:
User-directed 2026-07-29, from the user's own inquiry: "Can we stop using the mockup and instead use the real web app but feed the real web app with the fixture data, so we stop having to keep the mockup in sync with the real webapp?" The concrete cost being paid today is that `plans/layer2-mockup/` re-implements the File Nav, ruler, bubbles, drawer and diff pair in plain JS beside the real `webapp/` versions, so every approved mockup behaviour then has to be ported by hand — and the two do not line up: "the positioning of several items is not identical and reporting the differences is not worth the time or tokens".

DECISION (user, 2026-07-29): SERVER-SIDE stub routes, NOT a client-side static-data shim. `webapp/` is NOT touched by this task. That is the whole point of the choice — the page under review must be byte-identical to the production page, so the mockup and the app cannot differ in CSS, in component structure, or in the axis arithmetic. A client-side shim was considered and rejected here: it would add a branch to shipping client code and would still not fix positioning, because position comes from `webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts` and `webapp/layer1-styles.css`. (It would have had one extra payoff — a static GitHub Pages demo of the real page, which is what the now-closed task #17 originally wanted and what #222 wants to host. If that demo is ever wanted, it is a SEPARATE task built on top of this one, not a reason to change this one.)

THE SEAM, ALREADY BUILT. `dispatchLayer1Route` in jfred/src/viewer_server_layer1_routes.ts is a single function that owns every Layer 1 route and returns whether it OWNED the request, so the caller's chain falls through unchanged when it did not. Fixture mode is therefore ONE branch at the top of that function, routing to a fixture handler instead of the real ones. Note its header comment says "six HTTP routes" and it now dispatches EIGHT — POST `/api/layer1-settings`, GET `/api/layer1-settings`, `/api/layer1-view`, `/api/layer1-refs`, `/api/layer1-sessions`, `/api/layer1-file`, `/api/layer1-diff`, `/api/scan-source` — so fix that comment while you are in there. `/api/pick-folder` is registered in jfred/src/viewer_server.ts and does NOT go through the dispatcher; an OS folder dialog is meaningless against a fixture, so decide and document whether it stays live (harmless) or refuses in fixture mode.

THE WORK. (1) New jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture.ts holding the canned payloads for those eight routes. (2) One branch in `dispatchLayer1Route`. (3) A switch that is OFF by default and cannot be hit accidentally while looking at a real project — a `--fixture` argument to the viewer is the obvious shape; if a query param is used instead it must not be reachable from any link the normal page builds.

THE DATA. Translate `plans/layer2-mockup/fixture.js` — its `COMMITS`, `DISK`, `SESSIONS` and `SNAPSHOTS` arrays — into the wire shapes in jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts: `Layer1WireView` = { pairs, gitOrphans, diskOrphans, ruler }. Do NOT hand-compute the offsets: `Layer1WireInstant` carries `axisPx`, the S18 ruler ACCUMULATES, and `layOutNodeLadders` in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts is the one function the server and client already share to produce them — the fixture must go THROUGH it, or the page will disagree with itself the moment a folder filter re-lays out client-side. Carry the fixture's own invariants across, because they are what make the review meaningful: `born <= snapshot <= mtime`; one file carrying the same `@vN` from two different sessions with DIFFERENT bytes; one session carrying two `customTitle` values over two line ranges with a snapshot inside each; and a file with NO snapshots, which must render exactly as it does at Layer 1. The fixture also self-checks on load today — keep an equivalent assertion, since a fixture that violates its own rules is worse than no fixture.

THE HARNESS. Re-point jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts at the real page in fixture mode instead of serving `plans/layer2-mockup/` over `python3 -m http.server`. The 92 checks now in jfred/scripts/visual/mockup-checks.ts, mockup-checks-nav.ts and mockup-checks-diff.ts ARE the acceptance list for this task: a check that passed against the mockup and fails against the real page is either a real gap in the page or a mockup behaviour that was never ported, and each one must be classified as such rather than deleted. `scripts/visual/run.ts` (the existing six-state real-viewer loop) is the precedent for booting the server from a check script.

SCOPE LIMIT, DELIBERATE. Layer 2 does not exist in the real page yet — that is tasks #310-#318, none started. So fixture mode ships covering LAYER 1 ONLY, and `plans/layer2-mockup/` stays alive for Layer 2 review until roughly #315. It must not be deleted by this task. What this task buys immediately is that every FUTURE Layer 1 change is reviewed on the real page, and that #310-#318 are built against a page the user can actually see.

WHY IT BLOCKS #310 (user-directed 2026-07-29): the alternative was finishing all nine Layer 2 tasks in the mockup first, which would pay the porting tax nine more times — exactly the tax this task exists to stop.

VERIFY: `npm run viewer` with the flag serves /layer1.html rendering the fixture with no project folder, no git repo and no JSONL on disk; `webapp/` has zero changes in the diff; the flag off is byte-identical behaviour to today (a real project view is unaffected); the re-pointed check script runs green, with any check that could not be carried over listed and classified in the task's closure note rather than silently dropped.

title: Single-source the wire vocabulary that webapp/ re-declares from src/
description: User request 2026-07-29: solve the 'redeclared because webapp cannot import from src' issue with duplicated code. Maybe a build option that performs copies to the webapp/ folder? Known duplication sites (grep for 'cannot import from src' / 're-spelled' / 'Mirrors src/'): jfred/webapp/layer1-refs.ts:5 re-declares the /api/layer1-refs wire shape; jfred/webapp/layer1-source-paths.ts:7 re-spells SourceKind from src/structures/vocabulary.ts; jfred/webapp/layer1-sources.ts:8 re-spells CommitTimeSource (and notes Instant re-declared atop layer1-ruler-axis.ts); jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts:19 mirrors src/viewer_api_layer1.ts's listPairNodeLadder; jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts mirrors the Layer1Wire* shapes. Constraints discovered so far: webapp/ is compiled by tsconfig.webapp.json for the browser; webapp modules are ALSO loaded by node's type-stripping test runner, which rejects TS `enum` (so shared vocab must be const objects); the direction layer1-ruler-axis.ts already works — a webapp/ file imported BY src/ — is the existing precedent for sharing without copying. Candidate shapes to evaluate: (a) the user's suggestion, a build step that copies/generates the shared files into webapp/; (b) a shared folder both tsconfigs include (extending the layer1-ruler-axis precedent); note the repo rule against forwarding/re-export layers — one canonical home. This also serves plans/coding-requirements.md's 'single-source wire vocabulary' requirement.
